formulations.label: Nasal spray 0.1%
formulations.note: The clinic list gives no strength; this entry uses UK 0.1% nasal spray SmPCs (adults and children 12 years and over). A 0.05% product for children aged 6 to 12 years is a separate UK product with stricter contraindications (shown as detail items only).

src.q: Xylometazoline Hydrochloride 1 mg /1ml of solution
Nasal spray, solution (Nasal Spray)
Xylometazoline Hydrochloride 0.05% w/v

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Symptomatic relief of nasal congestion, perennial and allergic rhinitis (including hay fever) and sinusitis.

src.q: For the symptomatic relief of nasal congestion, perennial and allergic rhinitis (including hay fever), sinusitis.

items.t: The 2026 SmPC also names nasal congestion with the common cold, influenza and non-allergic rhinitis.

src.q: symptomatic relief of nasal congestion associated with the common cold, influenza, sinusitis, allergic and non-allergic rhinitis

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the two 0.1% spray SmPCs or the MHRA Drug Safety Updates accessed.

items.t: Adults and children 12 years and over: 1 spray into each nostril 1 to 3 times a day as required, for a maximum of 5 days. No more than 3 doses in 24 hours; leave at least 8 hours between doses (SmPC revised October 2026).

src.q: Adults and children 12 years and above: 1 spray into each nostril 1-3 times a day, as required, for a maximum of 5 days.
Maximum daily use: no more than 3 doses in any 24 hours. Leave at least 8 hours between doses

items.t: 0.1% spray SmPC revised 2024: adults and elderly, one application in each nostril up to 3 times daily; do not exceed 3 applications daily into each nostril.

src.q: Adults and elderly: One application in each nostril up to 3 times daily. Do not exceed 3 applications daily into each nostril.

items.t: Maximum duration: MHRA (April 2026) advises no use beyond 5 days; the maximum was changed from 7 to 5 days for adults and children 12 years and over. The 0.1% spray SmPC revised 2024 still says not more than 7 consecutive days; product information is being updated.

src.q: advise against prolonged or extended use beyond 5 days
The EAGs recommended changing the maximum duration of use from 7 days to 5 days in adults and children 12 years and above
Patients are advised not to take decongestants for more than seven consecutive days

items.t: 0.1% spray: contraindicated in children under 12 years.

src.q: Do not give to children under 12 years of age.
is contraindicated in children aged less than 12 years

items.t: MHRA (2009): cough and cold remedies containing nasal decongestants including xylometazoline should no longer be used in children under 6 years; products for 6 to 12 years are available from pharmacies only.

src.q: nasal decongestants (ephedrine, oxymetazoline, phenylephrine, pseudoephedrine, and xylometazoline)
Cough and cold remedies containing the above ingredients should no longer be used in children under 6 years
Products for children from 6 to 12 years will continue to be available in pharmacies where advice can be given.

items.t: Separate 0.05% child nasal drops (not the clinic form): contraindicated under 6 years; age 6 to 12 years under adult supervision, 1 or 2 drops in each nostril up to twice a day, not for more than 5 days without a doctor's advice.

src.q: Children between 6 and 12 years under adult supervision (all indications): 1 or 2 drops, in each nostril up to 2 times a day.
Not to be used for more than 5 days without the advice of a doctor.
Not to be used in children under the age of 6 years

items.t: Hypersensitivity to xylometazoline or to any excipient.

src.q: Known hypersensitivity to xylometazoline.
Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

src.q: Patients with trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy or surgery exposing the dura mater.
contraindicated in individuals with hypophysectomy or surgery exposing dura mater

src.q: Children under 12 years of age.

items.t: Taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors now or within the last 2 weeks.

src.q: This product is contraindicated in individuals who are taking or have taken monoamine oxidase inhibitors within the preceding two weeks.

items.t: Use with other sympathomimetic decongestants (oral or nasal), e.g. pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine, ephedrine.

src.q: Do not take with other sympathomimetic decongestants.
is contraindicated in patients who are taking other oral and nasal forms of sympathomimetic decongestants

items.t: The 0.1% spray SmPC revised 2024 (still the current text for that product) also lists: narrow-angle glaucoma; rhinitis sicca or atrophic rhinitis; phaeochromocytoma; prostatic hypertrophy. The SmPC revised in 2026 does not list these.

src.q: Narrow-angle glaucoma.
Rhinitis sicca or atrophic rhinitis.
Use in people with phaeochromocytoma, prostatic hypertrophy or those receiving monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI) treatment or who have received them in the last two weeks.

items.t: The separate 0.05% child drops SmPC is stricter: it also contraindicates cardiovascular disease including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, closed angle glaucoma, beta-blockers and inflammation of the nasal vestibule skin or mucosa.

src.q: Cardiovascular disease including hypertension Diabetes mellitus Phaeochromocytoma Prostatic hypertrophy Hyperthyroidism Closed angle glaucoma
Beta-blockers - (see section 4.5) Inflammation of the skin and/or mucosa of the nasal vestibule

items.t: Use with caution in coronary artery disease or other cardiovascular disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism and diabetes mellitus.

src.q: this product should be used with caution in patients suffering coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism or diabetes mellitus
Caution is recommended in patients with hypertension, cardiovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus or tri and tetra-cyclic antidepressant treatment

items.t: Long QT syndrome: may be at increased risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias.

src.q: Patients with long QT syndrome treated with xylometazoline may be at increased risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias.

items.t: Short-term use only. Overuse or use beyond the recommended time causes tachyphylaxis, rebound congestion and rhinitis medicamentosa; patients must stop treatment rather than increase the dose or extend treatment.

src.q: This medicine is intended for short term use only.
rebound congestion, rhinitis medicamentosa, and tachyphylaxis through overuse are recognised side effects
Patients must stop treatment rather than increasing the dose or prolonging treatment.

items.t: Use only with caution in patients who react strongly to sympathomimetics (insomnia, dizziness, tremor, cardiac arrhythmias or raised blood pressure).

src.q: should be used only with caution in patients showing a strong reaction to sympathomimetic agents as evidenced by signs of insomnia, dizziness, tremor, cardiac arrhythmias or elevated blood pressure

items.t: Contains benzalkonium chloride (SmPC revised 2024), which may irritate the nasal mucosa.

src.q: contains benzalkonium chloride. This may cause irritation of the nasal mucosa.

items.t: Other oral or nasal sympathomimetic decongestants (e.g. pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine, ephedrine): contraindicated together.

src.q: Do not take with other sympathomimetic decongestants.
do not use xylometazoline or oxymetazoline together or with other oral and nasal forms of medicines used to treat a blocked nose, such as pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine or ephedrine

items.t: MAO inhibitors (now or within 2 weeks): contraindicated; may raise blood pressure.

src.q: This product is contraindicated in individuals who are taking or have taken monoamine oxidase inhibitors within the preceding two weeks.
The concomitant use of xylometazoline with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors or tri- and tetra-cyclic antidepressants, may cause an increase in blood pressure

items.t: Tricyclic and tetracyclic antidepressants: may raise blood pressure; caution recommended (SmPC revised 2024).

src.q: The concomitant use of xylometazoline with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors or tri- and tetra-cyclic antidepressants, may cause an increase in blood pressure
Caution is recommended in patients with hypertension, cardiovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus or tri and tetra-cyclic antidepressant treatment

items.t: The SmPC revised in 2026 states that, because systemic absorption is low, interactions with medicines given by other routes are considered unlikely (no interaction studies done).

src.q: interaction with drugs administered via other routes is considered unlikely

items.t: The separate 0.05% child drops SmPC also lists: antihypertensives including beta-blockers (hypotensive effect may be blocked), cardiac glycosides (dysrhythmias), ergot alkaloids (ergotism), moclobemide (hypertensive crisis), appetite suppressants/amphetamine-like stimulants and oxytocin (hypertension).

src.q: Antihypertensives (including adrenergic neurone blockers & beta-blockers): Otrivine may block the hypotensive effects.
Cardiac glycosides : increased risk of dysrhythmias Ergot alkaloids (ergotamine & methylsergide): increased risk of ergotism
Moclobemide: risk of hypertensive crisis.

items.t: Renal impairment: normal adult dose (no specific studies in renal impairment).

src.q: Hepatic/renal dysfunction Normal adult dosage is appropriate
There have been no specific studies of this product or xylometazoline in hepatic or renal impairment.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: normal adult dose (no specific studies in hepatic impairment).

src.q: Hepatic/renal dysfunction Normal adult dosage is appropriate
There have been no specific studies of this product or xylometazoline in hepatic or renal impairment.

items.t: SPS: decongestants are not recommended at any stage of pregnancy (may reduce blood flow to the placenta and baby).

src.q: Decongestants are not recommended for use at any stage of pregnancy as they could reduce blood flow in the placenta and to the baby.

items.t: BUMPS: decongestant nasal sprays, drops or tablets should be avoided in pregnancy.

src.q: Ibuprofen and decongestant nasal spray, drops or tablets should be avoided in pregnancy.

items.t: SmPCs: one advises, as a precaution, not using in pregnancy because of possible systemic vasoconstriction; the other says not to use unless the benefit to the mother outweighs the risk to the fetus.

src.q: In view of its potential systemic vasoconstrictor effect, it is advisable to take the precaution of not using Otrivine during pregnancy.
This product should not be used during pregnancy unless the potential benefit of treatment to the mother outweighs the possible risks to the developing foetus.

items.t: No evidence of harm to the breastfed infant, but excretion in milk is unknown: use with caution and only on a doctor's advice (SmPC revised 2024). The 2026 SmPC: do not use unless the benefit outweighs the risk to the infant.

src.q: No evidence of any adverse effect on the breast-fed infant.
caution should be exercised and Otrivine should be used only on the advice of a doctor whilst breastfeeding
This product should not be used during lactation unless the potential benefit to the mother outweighs the possible risks to the nursing infant.

items.t: No fertility studies have been done; no information on effects on fertility.

src.q: No foetal toxicity or fertility studies have been carried out in animals.
There is no information on the effects of this product on fertility.

items.t: Common (SmPC revised 2024): headache, nasal dryness, nasal discomfort, nausea and application site burning. The 2026 SmPC lists headache as rare.

src.q: Nervous System Disorders Headache Common
Nasal Dryness Nasal Discomfort Epistaxis Common Common Uncommon
Nausea Common General disorders and administration site Application site burning Common
Nervous System Rare Headache

items.t: Rhinitis medicamentosa (the most serious overuse effect): persistent congestion and lasting changes to the nasal lining; severe cases may need surgery. Manage with gradual withdrawal, alternative treatment and follow-up.

src.q: rhinitis medicamentosa is the most serious of these reported effects
in severe cases, may require surgical intervention
Management may require a tailored treatment plan, including gradual withdrawal of the decongestant, use of alternative therapies, and clinical follow-up to monitor recovery

items.t: Hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema (very rare); irregular or fast heart rate (very rare).

src.q: Hypersensitivity reaction (angioedema, rash, pruritus) Very rare
Heart rate irregular Heart rate increased Very rare Very rare

items.t: Overdose or accidental swallowing: severe dizziness, sweating, very low body temperature, headache, bradycardia, hypertension (may be followed by hypotension), respiratory depression, coma and convulsions. Small children are more sensitive. Give supportive treatment and observe for several hours.

src.q: Excessive administration of topical xylometazoline hydrochloride or accidental ingestion may cause severe dizziness, perspiration, severely lowered body temperature, headache, bradycardia, hypertension, respiratory depression, coma and convulsions.
Small children are more sensitive to toxicity than adults.
This would include observation of the individual for several hours.

items.t: If congestion persists, worsens or does not improve after 5 days, stop and seek medical advice: alternative treatment may be needed.

src.q: if the symptoms of nasal congestion persist, worsen or do not improve after 5 days, alternative treatment may be required

items.t: Review patients who may have become reliant on the spray and advise gradual withdrawal; stopping abruptly can worsen symptoms; most recover within 3 months.

src.q: Opportunistically review patients who may have become reliant on using these products and advise them on how to gradually stop using these medications.
Stopping abruptly can worsen symptoms, but patients typically recover within 3 months with early recognition and treatment

items.t: For nasal use. Prime the pump before first use; re-prime if not used for more than 7 days (number of actuations depends on the pump type).

src.q: Before using for the first time, prime the pump by actuating 5 times.
if the product has not been used for longer than 7 days, the pump will need to be re-primed

items.t: Do not exceed the recommended dose, especially in children and the elderly.

src.q: The recommended dose should not be exceeded, especially in children and the elderly.

items.t: Use for a short time only: no more than 5 days in a row, do not exceed the daily dose and keep to the minimum time between doses.

src.q: do not use these medicines for more than 5 consecutive days
not exceed the daily recommended dose and to take note of the minimum time interval between doses

items.t: Do not use with other medicines for a blocked nose taken by mouth or into the nose, such as pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine or ephedrine.

src.q: do not use xylometazoline or oxymetazoline together or with other oral and nasal forms of medicines used to treat a blocked nose, such as pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine or ephedrine

items.t: Longer use can make the nose block again; talk to a healthcare professional if it is hard to stop, and see a doctor if symptoms worsen or do not improve after 5 days.

src.q: talk to a healthcare professional if you are having trouble stopping the medication
contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen or you do not feel better after 5 days, as you may need a different treatment
